senateStanding.note: On the University Senate's list of approved non–United Methodist schools of theology. A United Methodist candidate may attend here; the Senate list, not ATS accreditation, is the gate ¶324.4 names.

onlineCredit.note: GBHEM states that none of the Senate-approved non-UMC schools are approved to provide distance or online education for any classes in an M.Div., and that online or distance classes taken at them cannot count toward the educational requirements for UM ordination. Austin's M.Div. is an in-person degree, so this is less of a trap here than elsewhere — but it means an online course taken here for convenience is a course that does not count.

coverage.note: Introduction to Old Testament is a required course.
Introduction to New Testament is a required course.
Two required courses — Theology: Doctrines & Themes, and Theology: Figures & Movements.
Introduction to the History of Christianity: Apostolic Era to 1650 is required. Note the end date — a course stopping at 1650 does not touch Wesley.
Introduction to Preaching is a required course.
The Church as a Worshiping Community is a required course.
Theology & Practice of Mission & Evangelism is a required course.

Covered by the same single required course as mission. ¶324.4 asks for three semester hours in mission of the church in the world AND three in evangelism — one combined course may not satisfy both buckets. Ask your board before assuming it does.

This is a Presbyterian seminary; there is no United Methodist doctrine, polity, or history requirement, and ¶324.4 asks for a minimum of six semester hours. Partial help exists: Ángel Gallardo, assistant professor of church history, teaches a course on Methodism. That may serve the history component; nothing in the published curriculum covers UM doctrine or polity.

gapSummary: Austin Seminary covers seven of the nine ¶324.4 areas inside its required M.Div. curriculum, which is more than some United Methodist schools manage. The real gap is the six semester hours of United Methodist studies — doctrine, polity, and history — which a Presbyterian seminary has no reason to teach and does not.

Evangelism is a second, smaller question, because it shares a single required course with mission. Neither is a reason not to come here. Both are reasons to have the conversation with your Board of Ordained Ministry registrar before you enrol rather than in your final year, because the fix costs a semester if you plan it and a year if you do not.

gapRemedies.blurb: Take United Methodist studies online from a United Methodist school. GBHEM's restriction is on classes taken at the non-UMC schools; the thirteen UMC schools are all approved to deliver fully online coursework that counts. On the plain reading that makes an online UM doctrine/polity/history sequence from a UMC school the cleanest way to close this gap while you study in Austin — but confirm the arrangement with your registrar first, in writing.

Perkins offers the ¶324.4 studies as a nondegree track, Basic Graduate Theological Studies, built for exactly this situation. It is in Dallas, about three hours up I-35, and Perkins also teaches in Houston–Galveston.

Ask Dr. Gallardo what his Methodism course covers and whether it has been accepted for the UM history component before. He taught at Perkins before coming here, so he is likelier than most to know the answer.

Get it in writing from your conference's Board of Ordained Ministry registrar — which specific courses they will accept for United Methodist studies, evangelism, and mission of the church. A verbal yes from an admissions officer is not the same thing.

tuitionPerCredit.note: Austin states a three-credit course at $2,430, and the D.Min. residency session at $2,180. Be careful comparing this to other schools: Austin's own pages describe the M.Div. as 180 credits on one page and 78 on another, using different credit units. Ask for a total cost of the degree, not a per-credit figure.

pctReceivingAid.value: More than 90% of students receive some form of tuition assistance

typicalAward.value: Need-based grants up to 90% of tuition; eight merit scholarships cover full tuition
typicalAward.note: Austin also lists merit fellowships covering tuition, fees, and a housing/academic stipend, and says campus housing rent is subsidised at roughly half local market rate — which in Austin is not a small line item.

cost.honestNote: Austin publishes its federal loan default rate — 3.7% — which almost no seminary does voluntarily. Treat that as a real signal about how graduates actually fare, and as a fair question to ask any other school you are weighing.

degrees.name: Master of Divinity
degrees.blurb: The ordination degree, taught in person. Required courses run across Old and New Testament, history, two theology courses, ethics, Christian education, mission and evangelism, pastoral care, preaching, worship, world religions, and a senior capstone, plus a biblical language track and supervised ministry.
degrees.flag: Non-Presbyterian students take a one-language track rather than two

degrees.name: M.Div. / Master of Science in Social Work
degrees.blurb: Dual degree with UT Austin's Steve Hicks School of Social Work. Approved MSSW courses can satisfy M.Div. elective requirements — for agency ministry, advocacy, and clinical counselling.

degrees.name: M.Div. / Master of Business Administration
degrees.blurb: Dual degree with Schreiner University's online MBA in Ethical Leadership. Both degrees in four years, in residence at Austin.

degrees.name: Master of Arts in Youth Ministry
degrees.blurb: A dedicated youth ministry degree with its own director and research professor.
degrees.flag: All MAYM students receive a 100% tuition grant, regardless of need

degrees.name: Master of Arts (Theological Studies)
degrees.blurb: Not an ordination degree. Also carries the public theology concentration.

degrees.name: Certificado en Ministerio
degrees.blurb: A Spanish-language ministry certificate, alongside the Hispanic Ministries Mission Network. Not a degree, and not a route to ¶324.4 — but a real programme in Spanish.

partnerships.partner: The University of Texas at Austin, Steve Hicks School of Social Work
partnerships.blurb: The M.Div./MSSW dual degree. Approved social work courses count toward M.Div. electives — a genuine cross-registration, not just a marketing partnership.
The M.Div./MBA, pairing Austin's in-person M.Div. with Schreiner's 36-hour online MBA in Ethical Leadership over four years.
